dataSetInformation.common:generalComment: Dataset developed according to Arcadia project Methodology (Report: “Metodologia per gli studi di filiera della Banca Dati italiana LCA”). LCA study of electricity production from photovoltaic systems with 570 kWp of power (Report: “Filiera di produzione del mix elettrico italiano”). The dataset refers to the production of 1 kWh of electricity from photovoltaic systems with 570 kWp of power, in Italy, and it is representative of the processing technologies commonly used for this purpose.

referenceToExternalDocumentation.common:shortDescription:
Gabriella Fiorentino, Simona Scalbi, Antonietta Cerbone, Giuliana Ansanelli, Marco Giammartini, Amalia Zucaro. Filiera di produzione del mix elettrico italiano.
Background datasets from EcoInvent database cut-off (v.3.7.1) were used for the LCA study.

time.common:timeRepresentativenessDescription: This dataset has been considered valid until 2026, since no main changes have occurred in the electricity production from photovoltaic in the investigated years.

technology.technologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The dataset (1 kWh of electricity from photovoltaic IT, 570 kWp) refers to a system that includes all processes, from the extraction of raw materials to produce the photovoltaic panels up to the production of 1 kWh of electricity (cradle-to-gate approach), taking into account the 20-year life time of the system and the insolation received in the reference year (primary data). The primary data were provided by photovoltaic solar statistical report from GSE (Gestore Servizi Energetici, 2019), and by PVGIS software that calculates the insolation received. For the LCA study, background datasets from EcoInvent database 3.7.1 cut-off were used.
technology.technologicalApplicability: Electricity from Italian electricity mix sold to Italian electric grid.

dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.dataCutOffAndCompletenessPrinciples: Production of equipment and infrastructures is not included, except for the background system

referenceToDataSource.common:shortDescription: 20231031170512_Filiera di produzione del mix elettrico italiano.pdf

review.common:reviewDetails: The review was performed in compliance with Arcadia Metodology: “Metodologia per gli studi di filiera della Banca Dati italiana LCA” and ISO 14040-44 norms. The dataset has been assessed limited to the foreground data collected during the supply chain studies. Each dataset has been evaluated based on the following 4 criteria: 1. Technological Representativeness; 2. Time Representativeness; 3. Geographical Representativeness; 4. Reliability (A) In this context, the Reliability is very good.
review.common:otherReviewDetails: The study was judged by the reviewer as compliant with both ISO 14040-44 and Arcadia methodology.

referenceToFlowDataSet.common:shortDescription: Electricity from photovoltaic, 570 kWp, open ground installation, multi-Si, production mix at plant, Low Voltage

exchange.generalComment: In this class (570 kWp), all photovoltaic plants larger than 200 kWp are included. In this study, it is assumed that large PV plants are based on policrystalline silicon and open ground installation (30° inclination).

referenceToFlowDataSet.common:shortDescription: Photovoltaic plant, 570kWp, multi-Si, on open ground {GLO}| construction | Cut-off, U

exchange.generalComment:
The number of panels required to produce 1 kWh was calculated according to the following formula:
N. PANELS = 1/(570 kWp*T20* Ins_inclina_SI)
where 570 kWp is the power of the panel considered, T20 is the lifetime of the panel (20 years), Ins_inclina_SI (=1285.46 kWh) is the parameter of the annual electrical production from photovoltaics, calculated through the Photovoltaic Geographical Information System (PVGIS), wich evaluates the insolation value received by the type of cell considered

referenceToFlowDataSet.common:shortDescription: Tap water {Europe without Switzerland}| tap water production, underground water without treatment | Cut-off, U

exchange.generalComment: For panel cleaning, Ecoinvent assumes 20 L of water/year for m2 of installed panel (lifetime 30 years). The average surface area of a photovoltaic panel is assumed to be 1.65 m2 (https://www.sorgenia.it). The total amount of water was calculated as follows: (1,65*6,82E-8)*20*(20/30)
